column7: Employee names, job titles, and email patterns are publicly discoverable.
An external domain similar to the company name sends a targeted message to a finance employee.
Finance user successfully authenticates after opening the suspicious message. Sign-in risk is marked unusual.
A scripting engine launches from an Office-related process.
A new scheduled execution entry is configured to run when the user signs in.
A local protection setting is changed and later restored.
A privileged account authenticates on the workstation outside the administrator's normal pattern.
Security tooling reports an attempted access to stored credential material.
The workstation queries users, groups, nearby systems, shared folders, and domain resources.
The finance account connects to the file server using an unusual remote administration protocol.
Finance and customer export files are copied into a temporary staging folder.
The staged files are compressed into an archive with a generic name.
The workstation makes periodic encrypted web connections to a rare external domain.
A large encrypted outbound transfer occurs to an unfamiliar external service.
Many shared documents cannot be opened and file names have changed, disrupting business operations.
